newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Danny Boy may be silenced by European Commission.
newsitem.headline: Danny Boy may be silenced by European Commission.

text.p: The pipes that call Danny Boy -- symbol of the Irish diaspora -- may be silenced in the United States if the European Commission has its way.

Following a complaint by the Irish Music Rights Organisation (IMRO), the Commission on Monday said it was examining whether the U.S. contravened international trade laws by allowing bars and restaurants to play Irish music to customers.
The complaint centres on establishments which broadcast public television or radio stations featuring Irish music.
American television and radio stations pay a royalty fee to musicians whose records they play, but the owners of restaurants and bars are not obliged by American law to do so.
In Europe however, the Commission says any establishment which pipes music from broadcasters to its customers has to pay a licence fee which is distributed to performers.
An industry official admitted, however, that even in the EU this requirement is ignored or, at best, difficult to enforce.
The IMRO has told the Commission it is losing over one million dollars a year in royalties and that musicians in the 15-nation European Union were losing $30 million a year.

Under trade barrier regulations, the Commission will examine the complaint before deciding whether to ask member states to take the matter further. If it runs its course, the issue could become a matter for the World Trade Organisation to decide.
